items.title: trurl
items.author: Curator
items.content:
trurl is a command-line tool for parsing, constructing and modifying URLs in shell scripts.

It extracts individual components such as the hostname or path, replaces their values and resolves relative references. Query operations append parameters, remove matching keys and sort key-value pairs, with URL encoding handled by the parser.

It's URL handling is based on libcurl's parser, matching the interpretation used by curl. It reads batches of URLs from files or standard input and emits formatted components or JSON for further processing use cases.

For developers who are used to curl and writing shell scripts that prepare HTTP requests or clean URL lists, trurl provides structured operations for changing addresses and parsing URLs.

items.title: rustic
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rustic is a backup tool with a command-line interface for creating encrypted, deduplicated snapshots in the terminal.

It stores snapshots in local or cloud repositories using the same repository format as restic. Subsequent backups reuse existing data and record complete snapshots, while in-place restoration updates only changed files.

The interactive browser lists snapshots and their directory trees, with controls to edit tags and start restores. Configuration profiles define backup settings and retention policies for repeated runs.

For anyone that is interested in backups such as system administrators maintaining workstation or server backups, rustic works best for scheduled snapshots and interactive recovery from existing repositories.

items.title: rmpc
items.author: Curator
items.content:
rmpc is a terminal music client for Music Player Daemon (mpd) that browses music libraries locally and controls playback in your terminal.

It shows a three-column library browser which you can navigate the queue and supports choosing tracks, arranging the playback queue and managing saved playlists. If a track has the correct album metadata attached, rmpc will show the cover album artwork in terminals with compatible image protocols on the left hand side with the title and the artist name.

Whilst playing, rmpc will show the visualizer at the bottom and you can cycle through different visualizers as you navigate the queue. Synchronized lyrics are an extra addition and the panes can be configured to customize the view positions entirely such as optionally using cava for audio visualizations within the same interface.

For those who are listeners with an mpd setup, or looking for alternative local music players such as cmus or kew, rmpc can be useful as a feature rich media player for playing tracks and displaying album art and managing listening queues in the terminal.

items.title: tokui
items.author: Curator
items.content:
tokui is an interactive terminal viewer for exploring a codebase's size, language composition and complexity.

By default it runs tokei for line counts or uses an scc backend for complexity estimates from either code analysis tool. This tool comes with sortable tables and directory trees and treemaps of file attributes, such as line count, language and whitespace with a breakdown of how they are used or distributed in the code base.

tokui can be used as a command-line tool and integrates with Git to measure code churn, compare statistics between revisions and browse historical snapshots with side-by-side file diffs. Additionally, you can compose tokui to accept piped JSON as input and it can run an analysis on the codebase, which is useful for code reviews, CI automations and it gives helpful information of the total language use in a project.

For developers or software engineers who need to review and audit a project repositories code growth or learning a project's structure, tokui can be used for locating large directories and examining which folders have the most code distribution.

items.title: slackdump
items.author: Curator
items.content:
slackdump is a command-line archiving tool that saves Slack conversations and attachments without requiring admin-level privileges.

Using the interactive wizard in the terminal, it guides you to authenticate and export a given Slack workspace with SQLite archives and Slack-compatible ZIP exports available for accessible conversations. This tool can also view the exported archive inside which you can search the results afterwards.

It is possible to add newer messages through incremental updates in an existing archive and then open it in the built-in browser viewer or even convert it to static HTML. This tool comes with an MCP server which can gives AI tools and agents access to parsing the archived messages, conversations and threads for local analysis.

This tool is useful for team members who need to preserve project discussions or who are preparing for migration from chat platforms such as Mattermost or to another Slack workspace who need to. If you need other platforms, slackdump can also be used to migrate conversations to Discord.

items.title: sipnab
items.author: Curator
items.content:
sipnab is an advanced terminal tool for capturing and analyzing SIP signaling and RTP media to investigate VoIP calls at the packet level.

It reads live interfaces, packet capture files or HEP (Homer Encapsulation Protocol) feeds from SIP proxies, then it organizes messages into searchable dialogs and call-flow ladders. A split view places the decoded SIP message beside the sequence with a visual flow of each package type and the timeline in milliseconds.

sipnab does a low level RTP analysis that can reveal jittering in calls, packet loss and estimated voice quality for individual streams. HEP feeds carry signalling rather than call audio, so media analysis requires capturing the RTP traffic. Headless mode can export JSON and can be used for reports for automation.

Intended for VoIP engineers, system administrators or network engineers specialized in VoIP infrastructure, sipnab supports diagnosing failed call setups and one-way audio from captures on Linux and macOS.
